notes: Timings are incidental to this experiment and only indicative (shared 4-CPU machine).

Reference: shapely.contains_xy (interior only) and shapely.intersects_xy (interior or boundary). qoregeo's point_in_polygon() is ray casting with straight lng/lat edges, the same planar model as shapely.
A point counts as 'vertex' within 1e-12 deg of a vertex, as 'boundary' within 1e-12 deg of an edge, else 'numerical'.
public_vs_filter counts points where point_in_polygon() and filter_by_polygon() (an indexed implementation) give different answers.
Reference: the point is inside if (lng + k * 360, lat) is inside the continuous polygon for some k in -1, 0, 1 (shapely). qoregeo receives the point with its longitude in -180..180.
'continuous' rings use longitudes beyond +-180 (as buffer() does); 'split' is the same shape cut at 180 deg into a MultiPolygon (RFC 7946 section 3.1.9).
Seam points lie exactly on lng +-180 inside the physical shape. In the split form that meridian is a planar boundary of both parts.

Shape A ends at or crosses lng 180 (continuous longitudes); shape B starts at or just east of lng -180. Reference: shapely after moving B by -360, 0 or +360 deg; distance is the smallest of the three.
Reference: shapely.intersects (GEOS, exact predicates). Touching counts in both.

Regimes: random (both shapes in one window), touch (constructed contact at a vertex, on an edge, a shared edge or a collinear overlap), nested (inside a polygon or inside its hole), near (a touch pair moved apart by a gap of 1e-13 to 1e-5 deg).
Shape sizes (scale) are log-uniform from 1e-5 deg (about 1 m) to 10 deg.
Truth: geographiclib geodesic distance on WGS-84 <= radius. Test points come from Geodesic.Direct; their distance is recomputed with Geodesic.Inverse.
near_edge: geodesic distance uniform within +-1 % of the radius. area_uniform: uniform by area in a disk of twice the radius.
A haversine mismatch is 'explained by the sphere model' when an independent numpy haversine with R = 6371.0088 km gives the same in/out answer as qoregeo.

filter_by_line_50km_keeps: lng 179.9, 1 km from the short-way segment
notes: The README documents the planar long-way reading for polygon rings that jump across 180 deg (point_in_polygon) and says intersects() uses the same planar edges. length(), distance_to_line(), filter_by_line(), map() and image() read the same segment the short way.

Each set: points uniform in a longitude window centred between 150 and 210 deg, 0.01 to 300 deg wide; 20 % of the sets also get points at exactly lng 180 and -180. Expected framing: the narrowest covering longitude arc when it is under 180 deg wide (lng 180 and -180 are one meridian), else the raw min/max (a world map, the documented rule).
